frequency_question: How often does the Reserve Bank of India deploy incremental cash reserve ratios when liquidity management needs demand absorption within a defined calendar period?
membership_rule: Includes any formal monetary policy announcement or directive by the RBI implementing an incremental cash reserve ratio (iCRR) or temporary supplementary reserve requirement on scheduled banks. Excludes standard regular CRR adjustments.
provenance_note: 1 cases named, 2 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x); rate of 100% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 named major systemic liquidity surges requiring targeted absorption tools since 2000.
known_gaps: Excludes minor ad-hoc directive variations that did not carry the formal nomenclature of incremental reserve ratios.
skeleton: RBI monetary policy cycles involving unexpected liquidity overhangs where targeted temporary absorption tools are selected. Since 2000, major demonetization or post-pandemic liquidity surges represent distinct systemic episodes. Total major liquidity overhang episodes requiring extraordinary absorption: 2 instances (2016 post-demonetization incremental MSS/CRR variants, and 2023 iCRR).
multiplier: 2 historical systemic liquidity surge episodes where extraordinary ratio tools were deployed, out of 2 major liquidity overhang structural events, giving a high conditional implementation frequency when the principal's intent is activated.
validity_reason: Central bank statutory powers and operational frameworks regarding reserve ratios remain stable over multi-year horizons.
